 singapore 'Papa, can you do something?' Boy asks dad to help mousedeer in canal, NParks steps in to rescue it
 The mousedeer was spotted stranded in a canal in Bukit Panjang The mouse deer was seen stranded in a drain in Bukit Panjang and was seen bolting in the opposite direction when NParks officers approached it. PHOTO: Screengrab/Facebook/Ashz Loy PUBLISHED ON November 17, 2026 3:20 AM BY Swetha Sundararajan A seven-year-old animal lover's concern for a stranded mousedeer helped save the creature after he urged his father to call for help.
 The animal was rescued from a canal near Fajar Road in Bukit Panjang after officers from the National Parks Board (NParks) responded to the call.
 In a Facebook post on Thursday (Nov 12), Lee Ru Bing, 52, recounted how his son Ethan made the discovery while they were on their way to school at about 7am.
 From the car, Ethan spotted a small animal trapped in a deep drain and apparently unable to climb out.  
 "Papa, can you do something and rescue the poor little deer?", the boy asked, according to Lee.
 Lee, who described Ethan as an animal lover, said he wanted to help but was unable to enter the drain due to its depth.  
 After dropping his son off at school, he returned to the scene and contacted NParks for assistance. NParks responded quickly, dispatching two officers to the location.
 Videos shared by Lee showed the animal, later identified as a mousedeer, attempting to flee as one of the officers approached it inside the drain.
 The officer eventually secured the animal using a capture net and brought it to safety.
 Praising the officers for their swift response, Lee said Ethan was delighted to learn that the mouse deer had been successfully rescued.
 Another deer rescue 
 Just days before Ethan's discovery, another deer rescue drew attention from netizens.  
 A motorist travelling along the Bukit Timah Expressway (BKE) spotted a stranded sambar deer fawn on a grass verge on Nov 8.
 Together with a Land Transport Authority (LTA) officer, the motorist alerted NParks and the Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES).
 The fawn was subsequently rescued by NParks and taken to Mandai Wildlife Centre for treatment due to pre-existing health issues.
 After its condition stabilised, it was released into a forested area near where it had been found.
 Members of public who encounter injured, trapped or distressed wildlife may contact NParks' 24-hour Animal Response Centre at 1800 476 1600 for assistance.
